To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the editathon experience enabled participants to critically reflect on their own learning and their own agency, to develop an awareness of the gendered nature of Wikipedia, and to recognise the importance of Wikipedia in the construction of knowledge.

editathons can be used as a means of increasing critical awareness of the role of Wikipedia as a knowledge repository, and the gender inequities that exist within Wikipedia, and the Internet more broadly.

The participants' learning was primarily focused around three themes: a rewriting of history, the role of Wikipedia and traditional media in shaping society's information landscape, and the inter-play of the individual and collective in developing and sharing knowledge.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the learning experiences of participants of an edit-a-thon on Wikipedia.
how participants' learning experiences during the editathon have impacted their critical awareness of how information, knowledge and history is constructed and presented on the Internet.

how participants' experiences of the editathon enabled them to reflect upon their learning, and to critically engage with the ways in which Wikipedia is constructed, and how this is shaping society's access, engagement, and construction of knowledge.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Edinburgh Seven editathon was a successful intervention that provided participants with an authentic learning experience and a new critical understanding of the power of Wikipedia to shape how we engage with knowledge, and how this can be used to redress gender inequities.
editathons are a valuable learning experience that can be applied to a wide range of topics, particularly where the topic is underrepresented in the Wikipedia knowledge base.

the participants experienced a transformation from being passive consumers of information to active contributors of knowledge, which in turn enabled them to critically engage with the Internet as a medium for the production and dissemination of knowledge.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the participants' learning was a process of becoming, which was enabled by the editathon.
the participants learned how to edit Wikipedia and how to contribute to the shaping of history.
editathons are a useful tool to increase participants' understanding of the role of the Internet in constructing knowledge.
The main takeaway from our work is that
editathons can be a powerful tool in addressing gender inequities online and can provide participants with a sense of agency in shaping how we access and engage with information online.
the editathon is a powerful learning tool, which can be applied to many contexts to increase the diversity of voices on Wikipedia.

editathons can be a powerful learning opportunity to increase awareness of the role of technology, open resources, Wikipedia, and social media in shaping how we engage in information creation and consumption, and in constructing knowledge.
